title: GPU ABI drift investigation (scratchpad)
content:
Quick context:
- Notebook/replica nodes started throwing intermittent CUDA OOMs and mysterious loader errors after OS + driver patch on 2026-02-20. Symptoms only appear for some container images (older runtime stacks) and intermittently even for the same model.
- Hypothesis: ABI drift between host driver and libraries baked into container images (toolkit/runtime mismatch) + subtle caching/allocator differences causing spurious OOMs. Trying to capture breadcrumbs here (commands I ran, outputs, ideas).

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-02-20: kernel/drivers auto-update (driver moved from 525.x -> 535.x on some hosts).
- 2026-02-21: first customer-facing incident: model workers crash during long-running prompts.
- 2026-02-22: rolling restart of pool; some containers recovered, others still show errors.
- 2026-02-23..02-24: started collecting repros on both host and container.

Notes-to-self: core things to capture for SRE/ENG handoff:
- exact host driver (nvidia) version, kernel, module version
- libcuda.so symlink target(s) in container vs host
- output of ldd on problematic shared objects (libtorch_cuda.so, libcudart.so)
- nvidia-container-cli info, nvidia-smi snapshots around crash
- environment variables (LD_LIBRARY_PATH, CUDA_HOME, LD_PRELOAD)

Commands I ran (with key outputs):
1) nvidia-smi (host)
$ nvidia-smi -q -x | egrep "Driver Version|Product Name|FB Memory Usage"
Driver Version                        : 535.10
Product Name                          : NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
FB Memory Usage                       : Total                         : 40536 MiB

2) inside container: python small allocation loop (repro)
$ python -c "import torch; torch.cuda.init(); a = [torch.empty((1024,1024,256), device='cuda') for _ in range(8)]; print('allocated')"
=> sometimes crashes with: 
RuntimeError: unhandled system error: cudaGetDeviceProperties failed: unknown error
OR
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so: version 'NVIDIA_FATBIN_API_1' not found

3) ldd on offending module in container (example: libtorch_cuda.so)
$ ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | egrep -i 'cuda|nvidia|fatbinary|libcudart'
	libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so (0x00007f1a3c000000)
	libcudart.so.11.0 => /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0 (0x00007f1a3c400000)

But on some hosts the loader path resolves to an incompatible version (host lib vs container lib mismatch).

4) readlink /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so* (host vs container)
Host: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.535.10
Container (runtime mounts host lib): see that libcuda symlink points to .535.10 while the container ships libcudart from CUDA 11.2 runtime. Mismatch.

5) strace of the crash (truncated):
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
read(3, ... ) = 4096
...
dlopen("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so", RTLD_NOW) = NULL
dlerror() = "Version `NVIDIA_FATBIN_API_1' not found (required by /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so)"

6) nvidia-container-cli info (host)
$ nvidia-container-cli info --refsample /var/lib/docker/containers/<id>
- shows driver: 535.10, cuda version reported: 12.1
- plugin config: nvidia.runtime: "nvidia"

Observed patterns / oddities:
- Not every container image fails; newer images built from cuda:12.1-runtime base are fine. Older images baked against cuda:11.x fail more often.
- Failures can be "loader related" (missing fatbinary symbols) or true OOMs. Sometimes process logs show large reserved memory footprint from the allocator just before crash.
- On hosts with 525.x drivers we did NOT see these specific fatbinary errors (suggests new driver introduced new / different ABI symbol set).
- Some workloads hit OOM after many allocations (long-running), others fail early — likely a combination of ABI mismatch + allocator differences + fragmentation.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) ABI mismatch between host driver (libcuda.so) and container cudart/cupti libs -> deterministic loader error in certain code paths (fatbinary loader unresolved symbols). Explains loader errors patchy by image.
2) For OOMs: new driver changed memory behavior (reservation, prefetch, caching) leading to fragmentation with our allocator (custom caching allocator in runtime) on long-lived models.
3) Some kernel/driver combo has a regression causing spurious NVML reports and process termination (bus reset / GPU reset) under sustained allocation patterns.

Experiments done (and results):
- Rebuild image using cuda:12.1-runtime base -> problem disappears for that image on affected hosts. (Strong signal for hypothesis #1).
- LD_PRELOAD hack: tried LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so in container to force host loader binding -> suppressed loader error in one run but then crashed later with OOM. Not a long-term fix.
- Forcing container to use its own libcuda (copying host lib into image) -> made other symbols break (unexpected), so mixing libs is brittle.
- Reproduced with small allocation script (above) using different base images to confirm dependency.

Useful snippets to collect before remediation (capture on host and container):
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- modinfo nvidia | grep -E 'version|license'
- ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so* and inside container (if mounted)
- ldd on libtorch_cuda.so, libcudart.so in container
- python -m torch.utils.collect_env (saves a lot)
- dmesg | tail -n 200 around crash times (look for NVRM messages, GPU resets, page faults)
- /var/log/syslog around  time of crash

Immediate mitigations considered:
- Pin worker nodes to driver version 525 until we can roll images (rollback drivers via kernel/driver channel) -> high-cost and slow.
- Encourage rebuilds of critical images onto cuda:12.1 runtime (works but slow for many images).
- Add image check during deploy: run ldd on critical libs and check for 'fatbinary' / 'NVIDIA_FATBIN_API' mismatches and block if incompatible. Could be implemented in the CI gating step.
- Add runtime healthcheck in process supervisor that restarts on loader error and dumps full diagnostics to S3 (nvml, ldd, env).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there a user-facing impact curve (i.e. increased cost due to retries) we can quantify quickly? (ask CS for example traces).
- Could the allocator changes in recent PyTorch builds interact badly with driver 535? Try reproducer with specific PyTorch wheel versions.
- Can we get the exact symbol/version mapping from driver 535 vs 525 to create a minimal compatibility matrix? (nm/objdump on libnvidia-fatbinaryloader?).
- Is there a way to ask NVIDIA about NVIDIA_FATBIN_API versioning (support ticket)?

Next actionable steps (short):
- [ ] Collect collect_env output from 3 failing containers and 3 working containers (Maya to help).
- [ ] Add automated ldd/version check to image CI for all model-serving images (me).
- [ ] Prototype small shim that detects loader error at process start and logs full diagnostics (Diego).
- [ ] Open support ticket with NVIDIA with minimal reproducer and strace/nm outputs.

Notes to future me: when you see "libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so: version 'NVIDIA_FATBIN_API_1' not found" think: host driver newer than the binary ABI expected by user-space modules. Fix by aligning runtime/toolkit or upgrading compiled artifacts. Also remember that LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH are fragile in containerized runtime with modern nvidia-container-toolkit because it mounts host libs at runtime.

Misc scraps (throwaway logs I saved):
- PyTorch stderr snippet:
  RuntimeError: CUDA error: unknown error
  CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call,so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.

- dmesg around a crash:
  [ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0002:65): PID=1, GPU=00000000:81:00.0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [ 12346.000100] nvidia: GPU at 00000000:81:00.0 is lost.

If/when this lands in a formal incident writeup, include: clear repro steps, exact image IDs, host kernel+driver, ldd outputs for critical libs, strace of dlopen failure, and the observed mitigation (rebuild on compatible base).

End of scratchpad.

(Notes intentionally terse — meant as breadcrumbs for follow-up.)
